evidence: The candidate states that malformed JSON causes `current` to become a partial/zero config and readiness false, then requires preserving version 7 and readiness while exposing failure separately.

It requires candidates to be “fully decode[d] and validate[d]” but does not explicitly require every semantic rule: positive version, non-empty wildcard-free origins, all positive route limits, and non-empty TLS server name.
It identifies the post-`Store` mutation of `AllowedOrigins[0]` as racing with `Policy` and changing authorization, and requires published slices/maps to remain immutable.
It explicitly says writing `TLSClientConfig` races with concurrent transport use and notes that reused version-7 connections can produce inconsistent TLS behavior.
It requires atomically publishing a generation containing immutable policy/config and its immutable round tripper, acquired once per operation for authorization, limits, version, and TLS.
It requires serialized or CAS-based admission/publication, rejects lower and conflicting same-version candidates, and makes equivalent same-version candidates a no-op.

It assigns old generations only to already-admitted operations and calls for generation-bound pools, but does not explicitly require retiring obsolete idle connections without disrupting in-flight work.
It requires preserving readiness and separately recording reload failure, but does not establish a bounded operational success/failure signal.
The candidate condemns post-publication slice mutation as a race; it does not claim `atomic.Pointer` makes it safe.
The candidate condemns mutation of `TLSClientConfig` on the shared in-use transport as a race.
The candidate condemns clearing readiness after a failed reload and requires readiness to remain unchanged while version 7 serves.
The candidate rejects last-writer-wins, requiring lower versions and conflicting duplicates to be rejected.
The candidate identifies separate config and transport updates as a mixed-generation bug and requires one atomic snapshot cutover.
verdict.summary: The response catches the central publication, ordering, immutability, readiness, and shared-transport defects. It falls short of explicitly enumerating every required semantic validation rule, explicitly retiring obsolete idle connections, and requiring a bounded reload-status signal.
